full_judgment:
13. Among the 15 PWs examined PW 1 Sk Saber Ali is the informant. He was Senior Post Master of Dhaka General Post Office at the relevant time. He supported the prosecution case giving details of the procedure of opening ordinary savings account, conversion of such account as a cheque account, withdrawal of money from such cheque account, opening of the questioned ordinary account on 19-9-1979 on deposit of Taka 100 only in the name of Oliur Rahman of 9, Shantinagar, Dhaka, a non-existent/fictitious person, conversion of such account as a cheque account on 9-1-1980 on the basis of an application showing balance of Taka 35,100 in the account, making of interpolation in the ledger book, withdrawal of money from the questioned account on different dates and part played by the accused persons in doing those. 

 34. It is in the evidence of PW 1 that the signature of the account holder in all the cheques were identical with the specimen signature preserved with the index-card. So, it appears that Kazi Shamsul Alam after comparing the signature of the account holder in the cheques with the specimen signature finding those identical submitted the cheques to the Assistant Post Master who passed the cheque and accordingly, payment was made. Thus, on scrutiny of the evidence on record, we find substance in the submission of Mr Mahbub Ali, the learned Advocate for the appellant of Appeal No. 815/1987. Only because Kazi Shamsul Alam worked as signature comparing clerk and payment clerk on the aforesaid three dates of withdrawal of money he cannot be convicted. It may be mentioned here that there is no evidence that Kazi Shamsul Alam was an author of any interpolation in any paper or connected with causing disappearance of evidence or committing forgery and criminal breach of trust by removing the relevant page of the ledger book. So, it is a case of no evidence against him. His conviction is not based on legal evidence, but on surmise and conjecture. On the above reasons we are of the view that the prosecution failed to prove the charge under sections 409, 467 and 201 of the Penal Code against Kazi Shamsul Alam and, as such, he is entitled to get acquittal honorably of the charge under those sections.
